verses.text: I don't really need to write to you about this service for God's people,
because I know you're ready to help. I've been boasting about you to the Macedonians, saying that Achaia has been ready since last year. Your enthusiasm has stirred up many of them.
Still, I'm sending the brothers so our boasting about you won't turn out to be empty talk. As I said, I want you to be ready.
Otherwise, if some Macedonians come with me and find you unprepared, we'd be embarrassed—let alone you—after being so confident in you.
So I thought it was necessary to urge the brothers to visit you ahead of us and prepare the generous gift you promised. Then it will be ready as a generous gift, not something given reluctantly.
Remember: whoever sows sparingly will also harvest sparingly, and whoever sows generously will also harvest generously.
Each of you should give what you've decided in your heart—not reluctantly or because someone pressures you. God loves a cheerful giver.
God can pour every kind of grace into your lives, so that you'll always have everything you need and plenty left over for every good work.
As Scripture says, ‘They freely give to the poor; their righteousness lasts forever.’
The one who supplies seed to the farmer and bread to eat will supply and multiply your seed for sowing and increase the harvest of your righteousness.
You'll be made rich in every way so you can be generous on every occasion, and your generosity will result in thanksgiving to God through us.
This service of giving does more than meet the needs of God's people; it also overflows in many thanksgivings to God.
Because of the way you serve, people will praise God for your obedience to the Good News of Christ and for your generous sharing with them and everyone else.
And as they pray for you, they'll long for you because of the extraordinary grace God has shown you.
Thanks be to God for his gift beyond words!
